articleTitle: The role of advisory systems in control systems simulation and design
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Knowledge-Based Control: Principles and Applications
abstract: An advisory approach has been taken to the development of two prototype knowledge-based systems for the simulation and design of multi-input multi-output control systems. The Control System Simulation Adviser (CSS-Adviser) and the Control System Design Adviser (CSD Adviser) were developed on the belief that they were not to initiate any operation without the user's approval. However, during most of the simulation or design process, they can guide the user in making the necessary decisions, help him interpret results, and discover errors which may arise.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Knowledge-based control of a binary distillation column
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Knowledge-Based Control: Principles and Applications
abstract: Implementing a process model using fuzzy methods has proved successful when considering the steady state determined models based controller algorithm of Davison, and has given a much improved performance when compared to a design based on average process gains only. With the addition of dynamic response and process dead time compensation inherent in the self organising process at the highest level it is then possible to provide a direct and straightforward approach to tuning and adaptation of model based control algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Application of COGSYS to real-time process control
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Knowledge-Based Control: Principles and Applications
abstract: COGSYS is a real-time knowledge-based system which can function as a SCADA (Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition) system, but with a more structured development language, declarative and procedural knowledge instead of just procedural, and extra levels of processing. It was used at British Gas in conjunction with an existing PID (proportional, integral and derivative) control system on a methanator feedgas production plant. Four main areas were covered: control optimisation; condition monitoring; procedures; and alarm interpretation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On-line self-organizing fuzzy logic controller with patient simulators
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Knowledge-Based Control: Principles and Applications
abstract: The development of online drug administration strategies in operating theatres represent a highly safety-critical situation. The usefulness of different levels of simulation prior to clinical trials has been shown in previous studies in muscle relaxant anaesthesia. In the present approach the control software was implemented on the actual machine to be used in theatre, while another computer acted as a real-time patient simulator. The paper illustrates the usefulness of the controller/simulator approach via results of scale-factor selection, choice of self-organising fuzzy logic control rule-base, and the effect of the drug sensitivity scheduler.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A framework for knowledge based process control
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Knowledge-Based Control: Principles and Applications
abstract: Numerical control algorithms have a firm theoretical basis and a small class of algorithms typified by the three term controller is well accepted in the process industry. The basis for continuing to apply such algorithms is that in a well tuned form they often exercise excellent control and are robust in the face of certain changes in the process. In this context, the role of knowledge based control is in the supervision of closed loop controllers based on traditional algorithms.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Physics and linguistics of technical and social control systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Knowledge-Based Control: Principles and Applications
abstract: More recently, there has been a demand for theoretical description of purposive assemblies of technical, biological and socio-economic nature consisting of functional objects connected according to a specific topology. As far as technical assemblies are concerned, this demand has been met by the various approaches to control systems analysis which seem to have a number of disadvantages. The objective of this paper is to describe through examples illustrating the generalised description: (1) an alternative approach to the analysis of technical (and natural) situations based on a mathematical description, which can evolve into a description of technical control systems; and (2) an approach based on a linguistic description applicable to the qualitative and quantitative analysis of socio-economic as well as technical assembling.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Implementation of a self-organising computer vision control system
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Knowledge-Based Control: Principles and Applications
abstract: The authors describe the application of a self-organising computer vision control system for fibre quality monitoring at hardboard mills. The system provides a continuous measurement of fibre quality and uses the rule-based controller to advise the machine operator to alter the refiner settings.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Practical aspects of rule and knowledge based control
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Knowledge-Based Control: Principles and Applications
abstract: The paper is based on experience gained in the installation and commissioning of the LINKman rule based control system in cement plants and other industries. However despite the success of these techniques in cement the number of such systems in use outside the cement industry is still very small. One reason appears to be concern about plant safety. The paper addresses this issue and then reviews the factors upon which the success of a project depends.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The architecture of knowledge bases required for implementing expert control systems
publicationTitle: IEE Colloquium on Knowledge-Based Control: Principles and Applications
abstract: The process of control system is a well understood, structured and iterative process. One form of real time control involves real time design and in this approach to expert control the controller is designed or updated on a real time basis. It is this approach to expert control that is considered. A general knowledge base structure for expert control based on the 'blackboard' concept and object oriented design has been suggested.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
